Before you click an answer, plug it back in. And when the answer is at an edge number, test the edge itself.
Think of it as checking your work before you hand it in. It takes ten seconds and catches the mistakes that cost points.
Two choices often look right. Plugging in decides between them in seconds.
Which line has slope negative one half and passes through four, one? Both y equals negative one half x plus one, and y equals negative one half x plus three, have the right slope.
Plug in x equals four. Negative one half times four plus one is negative one. Not one. Negative one half times four plus three is one. That's the line.
Edge numbers. Three k plus ninety is less than zero. What is the greatest possible integer k? Solve: k is less than negative thirty.
Test the edge. Three times negative thirty plus ninety is zero. Is zero less than zero? No. With less than, the edge doesn't count. So step one past it: negative thirty one.
Let's try an SAT style question. Two times x plus three equals two x plus k has no solution. Which could be k?
The left side is two x plus six. If k were six, both sides would be identical, and every x would work. That's infinitely many solutions, not none.
So k can be anything except six, like five. Then two x plus six equals two x plus five, which is never true. No solution.
Your turn. Pause the video. x plus four is greater than ten. What is the smallest integer x?
x is greater than six. Test six: six plus four is ten, and ten is not greater than ten. So the answer is seven.
Remember three things. Plug your answer back in. Test the edge number itself. And with less than or greater than, the edge doesn't count. Great work.
